1.d4 f5 2.e4 fxe4 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bg5.strategy: The main line: the bishop attacks the knight that defends e4, threatening to take it and win the pawn back with Black's structure damaged. It also keeps the queen's check on h5 in reserve for when the knight goes. Black has to answer the threat precisely.
1.d4 f5 2.e4 fxe4 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bg5.name: Dutch Defence: Staunton Gambit
1.d4 f5 2.e4 fxe4 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bg5.background: The main line of the gambit. Staunton first played 4.Bg5 in the London game against Horwitz in 1846.

1.d4 f5 2.e4 fxe4 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.f3.strategy: Offers a second pawn to open the centre and bring the pieces out with tempo. Taking it with ...exf3 gives White real compensation, so Black does better to strike back in the centre at once and keep the extra material.
1.d4 f5 2.e4 fxe4 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.f3.name: Dutch Defence: Blackmar's Second Gambit

1.d4 f5 2.e4 fxe4 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.g4.strategy: Throws the g-pawn forward to drive the f6 knight away with g5, but it loosens the cover in front of White's own king while White is still a pawn down. The quiet ...h6 takes the point out of it, and White does not have enough for the pawn.
1.d4 f5 2.e4 fxe4 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.g4.name: Dutch Defence: Staunton Gambit, Tartakower Variation

1.d4 f5 2.e4 fxe4 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bg5 c6.strategy: Prepares the central strike ...d5 with a pawn behind it: played at once, that strike would run into a tactic on the weakened kingside, while with the c-pawn in support it works. Black accepts that White may regain the pawn and plays for a solid game.
1.d4 f5 2.e4 fxe4 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bg5 c6.name: Dutch Defence: Staunton Gambit, Chigorin Variation

1.d4 f5 2.e4 fxe4 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bg5 g6.strategy: Shuts the h5-e8 diagonal for good and prepares to fianchetto the bishop, so the king gets the safety the gambit was aimed at. The cost is the h6 square, which the g5 bishop already attacks, and the e4 pawn is still hard to hold.

1.d4 f5 2.e4 fxe4 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bg5 b6.strategy: Prepares ...Bb7 as a second defender of the e4 pawn, so Black tries to keep the extra pawn instead of returning it. The cost is time: Black spends a move on the queenside while the g5 bishop presses on f6 and the king's side stays open.
1.d4 f5 2.e4 fxe4 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bg5 b6.name: Dutch Defence: Staunton Gambit, Nimzowitsch Variation
